study type: Cross-sectional study with a longitudinal follow-up in a subgroup
exposure: Circulating agonistic autoantibodies at the angiotensin-II type 1 receptor (AT(1)-AA)
outcome: Circulating agonistic autoantibodies at the angiotensin-II type 1 receptor (AT(1)-AA) positivity
cohort: The study included 41 women (24 with preeclampsia, 17 normotensive controls) who underwent elective cesarean section.
finding: Circulating AT(1)-AA were significantly more often present in women with preeclampsia than in normotensive pregnancy at delivery, however, no significant correlation was found between uteroplacental acute atherosis and circulating AT(1)-AA at delivery.
